bullets.title: Fed turns hawkish: 9 of 18 dots signal 2026 hike; markets reprice 36bp of tightening
bullets.body: The June FOMC held rates at 3.50-3.75% but stripped forward guidance and showed a hawkish dot plot tilt—9 of 18 members project at least one 2026 rate hike, pushing market pricing to 36bp of hikes through year-end from 19bp pre-decision. Chair Warsh emphasized price stability; Morgan Stanley argues the SEP inflation forecasts look too aggressive given the Iran deal oil relief and expects the Fed on hold through year-end, while 22V flags core PCE at or below ~0.21% monthly as the pivot threshold before renewed tightening risk.

bullets.title: Treasury curve flattens sharply: 2Y +9bp, 30Y -7bp; foreign demand for Treasuries recovering
bullets.body: Post-FOMC curve flattening was significant—2Y yields rose 9bp to ~4.20% while 30Y fell 7bp to ~4.90%. Foreign investors bought a net $50.5bn in long-term Treasuries in April (highest since Nov 2025), with Japan and China both recording net purchases for the first time since January. JPMorgan reduced its 2026 foreign demand forecast from $500bn to $450bn; technically the 30Y targets 4.80-4.82% as the richer end, with 4.95-4.98% as tactical support.

bullets.title: US-Iran peace deal reopens Strait of Hormuz; WTI down ~30% in a month, below $77
bullets.body: A US-Iran MOU was signed this week, lifting the Hormuz blockade and potentially adding ~1M bpd of Iranian exports over 2-3 years; UAE and Saudi Arabia could produce above pre-war levels by 4Q26. WTI crude is down ~10.6% on the week and ~30% over the past month to below $77, with US average gas prices falling below $4/gallon for the first time since March. Lower oil is structurally positive for tech, discretionary, and communications per 22V, while JPM's energy monitor shows retail fuel prices down 4% in June with further declines expected.

bullets.title: Narrow AI rally drives Nasdaq +2.6% WTD vs S&P +1%; breadth at 3rd percentile
bullets.body: The week's equity gains were highly concentrated—only ~30% of stocks outperformed (3rd percentile breadth), with semis up 7.3% and DRAM up 18% leading Nasdaq to +2.43% WTD. Levered ETF exposure is near record highs with ~$20bn per 1% SPX move in short gamma, and an estimated $26bn rebalancing demand hit on Friday. Macro systematic strategies (Vol Target/CTA/Risk Parity) supplied ~$90bn over the past month and sit at 45th percentile leverage; US L/S gross leverage hit 98th percentile at 213%.

bullets.title: AI FOMO trade: 75% of mutual funds underweight semis; options skew flat despite record positioning
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley flags that 75% of US mutual funds remain below benchmark weight in semis despite the sector now comprising ~25% of S&P index weight. 32% of global hedge fund net leverage sits in semis (vs. 5% in 2023) yet nearly 20% of hedge funds have <10% AI exposure. US implied vols on semis are at 40v vs. 16v realized average; MS recommends low-premium call-spread collars and worst-of structures on NVDA, MSFT, GOOGL, META, AVGO to manage FOMO-driven chase risk.

bullets.title: Capital markets boom: IPOs +415% YoY, equity issuance +117%, M&A +64% in 2Q26 QTD
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley's deal dashboard shows a broad capital markets surge in 2Q26—equity issuance up 117% YoY led by North America at +234%, IPOs up 415% YoY, and annualized M&A up 64% with sponsor trends flipping positive. This surge in activity creates a significant earnings tailwind for investment banks and validates risk-on positioning.

bullets.title: USD setup bullish: DXY targets 105.74 breakout; gold risks medium-term reversal below 4030-4074
bullets.body: JPMorgan FX technical strategy sees the DXY threatening a breakout from a 2025-2026 base pattern with a 105.74 measured move objective if sustained above 98.71-98.93 support, now supported by decelerating industrial metals and precious metals distribution patterns. EUR/USD shows a maturing bearish reversal below 1.20 with downside targets at 1.111-1.1185 on a break of 1.134. Gold's break below 4030-4074 would confirm a medium-to-longer-term bearish reversal.

bullets.title: Housing starts weakest since 2020 at 1.177M; multi-family collapsed 42%
bullets.body: Housing starts printed at 1.177M vs. 1.430M expected—the lowest since 2020—driven by a 42% drop in multi-family starts. This compares unfavorably against the hawkish Fed backdrop with 30Y mortgage rates pressured by the curve. Pending home sales did beat at +3.8% vs. +0.9% consensus, providing a partial offset.

bullets.title: FERC accelerates data center grid interconnections; co-location tariff approved; 90-day fast-track
bullets.body: FERC approved PJM's revised co-location tariff allowing data centers to contract only for incremental grid load above on-site generation, and issued show-cause orders to RTOs to accelerate connections beyond the 2029 target on a 90-day timeline. Data centers must fund infrastructure upgrades. Texas PUCT approved Batch 0 load forecasting for ERCOT with 35 GW baseload and 65 GW under study; clarity on project inclusion expected by August 7, benefiting IPPs including TLN, CEG, and VST.

bullets.title: $130B in data center projects blocked in 2026 by public opposition; incumbents insulated
bullets.body: $130B in data center projects are blocked or delayed in 2026 due to pushback on power, water, and community impact—particularly in Texas. Data center REIT incumbents like Equinix and Digital Realty appear insulated from opposition relative to new entrants. Hyperscalers face escalating grid upgrade costs and local ratepayer pushback while FERC fast-tracks approvals.

bullets.title: OpenAI's $600B capex plan faces margin credibility gap; S-1 will be a key stress test
bullets.body: 22V Research flags that OpenAI's Q1 2026 gross margin was ~39%, well below the 50%+ hyperscaler comp level needed to support its $600B capex commitment (including a $300B Oracle compute deal from 2027). Even the most optimistic scenario (81% peak GM) supports only ~$500B in capex; token price compression or slower ad revenue could open funding gaps. The forthcoming S-1 will test whether margin acceleration assumptions are achievable.

bullets.title: Apple confirms unavoidable price hikes as memory costs 4x higher YoY; iPhone ASP up ~$50 per JPM
bullets.body: Tim Cook confirmed Apple will raise product prices citing a surge in DRAM/NAND costs that are 4x higher year-over-year. Press estimates of $200+ ASP increases are aggressive; JPM models only ~$50 increases for iPhone 18 (mid-single-digit %) after accounting for ~$40 in component savings and ~$15 from modem vertical integration. US carriers are unwilling to absorb subsidy cost increases, shifting burden to consumers with unit demand risk.

bullets.title: ECB likely one more hike despite Iran oil deal; Euro area inflation sticky above 3% headline through early 2027
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects one more ECB rate hike given sticky inflation—May HICP at 3.2% headline and 2.6% core with services surging 0.49% m/m. Even the ECB's 'mild' scenario shows inflation above 3% headline and 2.5% core through early 2027. Flash PMIs and IFO data next week are key inputs to timing. Separately, JPMorgan shifted the BoE hike forecast to November from July after UK CPI surprised to the downside at 2.8% YoY.

bullets.title: Consumer traffic decelerating broadly in 2Q26; retail geolocation data softening across hardlines
bullets.body: KeyBanc's hardlines traffic index declined -1.1% week-ending June 14. Most major retailers decelerated from 1Q to 2Q: WMT slowed 200bps to +0.7%, LOW fell to -0.8%, TGT slowed 270bps to +4.2%, and FIVE saw the largest deceleration at -780bps to +17.9%. MUSA was the standout exception, improving 500bps to +7.2%. The broad deceleration pattern is consistent with Oppenheimer's warning that tariff-driven price hikes will pressure discretionary spending.

bullets.title: ADP 4-week average slows to +25.5k; jobless claims 229k above consensus; hiring muted by AI concerns
bullets.body: UBS notes ADP's 4-week average hiring fell to +25.5k from +29.0k, with muted hiring broadly attributed to AI-driven uncertainty. Weekly jobless claims came in at 229k vs. 220k expected; UBS expects claims to move higher. Mortgage applications declined 3.8% week-over-week, consistent with housing starts weakness.

bullets.title: Banxico holds at 6.5%; Mexico 1Q GDP contracted 2.4% SAAR; JPM forecasts 1.0% full-year growth
bullets.body: JPMorgan expects Banxico to hold rates unanimously at 6.5% with a slightly more dovish tone as June CPI is forecast to fall to 3.67% YoY—the lowest since December 2025 and within the 2-4% target band. Mexico's 1Q26 GDP contracted 2.4% seasonally annualized with consumption and investment both falling, though April IGAE is expected to show a 0.6% monthly bounce. JPM forecasts 1.0% real GDP growth for full-year 2026, up from 0.6% in 2025, with the World Cup expected to boost tourism and consumption in 2H.

bullets.title: AI regulatory environment tightening: Commerce Dept. suspends Anthropic foreign access; federal legislation likely in 2027
bullets.body: The Commerce Department ordered Anthropic to suspend foreign access to Claude Fable 5 and Mythos, marking an escalation in AI containment policy. Federal AI legislation is seen as more viable in 2027, with data center power costs and financial stability as key congressional focus areas. Congress is being urged to study how correlated AI agents could amplify market volatility; a massive cyber or AI-enabled disruption event could accelerate legislative action.

bullets.title: Wells Fargo raises S&P 500 year-end PT to 7,950; Street forecasting ~22% Q2 earnings growth
bullets.body: Wells Fargo lifted its year-end S&P 500 price target to 7,950 from 7,300, consistent with the S&P trading up for 11 of the past 12 weeks and within ~1.5% of its June 2 record. The Street is forecasting ~22% Q2 earnings growth. JPMorgan flags AI capex depreciation expenses as a potential headwind to future earnings growth as hyperscaler build-outs mature.

bullets.title: Key macro catalysts next week: PCE (Jun 25), PMIs (Jun 23), MU earnings (Jun 24)
bullets.body: The macro calendar is dense next week: PCE Price Index prints June 25 as the key inflation read against the Fed's hawkish SEP; flash PMIs on June 23 will test growth assumptions; and MU reports June 24 with semis up 7.3% WTD setting a high bar. The mandatory USMCA joint review is due July 1, and the one-year Trump-Xi trade truce expires November 1.

bullets.title: Brent below $80 post-Iran deal; EM Edge inflation plateauing at 6.5% YoY; food price risks from El Niño in 4Q26-1Q27
bullets.body: Brent crude falling sharply below $80/bbl following the US-Iran peace deal; global CPI has leveled at 3.5% YoY with EM Edge averaging 6.5% YoY. Inflation momentum has plateaued in Asia and Africa but risen in LatAm to its highest since mid-2022. Food prices are broadly tame but El Niño risks in 4Q26-1Q27 could trigger upside surprises, particularly in southern/southeastern Africa and Central America through drought effects.
